readings.title: The garden rota with empty spaces
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Hilltop Garden asked each member to sign up for a weekly watering duty. The first rota assumed that everyone could visit on a fixed weekday. Several members with changing work hours missed turns and felt unwelcome. The group introduced paired duties and a board on which members could exchange times. It also provided seated tasks such as sorting seeds. Plants received more regular attention, while members contributed in different ways. Equal membership did not require identical physical work. The group still recorded tasks so that flexibility did not leave essential jobs invisible.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The crop that surprised the class
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A growing class planted the same bean variety in two containers. One was near a wall and the other beside an open fence. The wall-side plants grew taller, but a learner warned against crediting the soil mixture immediately. Light, wind and watering might also differ. The class moved to a more controlled comparison for its next planting and kept notes on both successes and failures. The first result remained interesting, but it could not isolate a single cause. Curiosity improved the project when it led to a better question rather than an impressive claim.

readings.title: Who takes the tomatoes?
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A shared garden had no written rule about harvesting. Early visitors often picked the ripe tomatoes, leaving little for those who came after work. Nobody had intended to be unfair, but resentment grew. Members agreed to place part of each harvest in labelled boxes for later collection and leave another part for immediate use. The arrangement added a small task for whoever picked first. In return, people could see how the crop was being shared. A productive garden had revealed a social problem that watering and good soil alone could not solve.

readings.title: A balcony's weight problem
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Ravi wanted to cover his small balcony with large planting containers. Before buying them, he asked the building manager about permitted loads and drainage. He learnt that wet soil weighed much more than he had expected and that water could drip onto a neighbour's balcony. Ravi chose fewer lightweight containers and trays, leaving access to the door clear. His garden looked less like the photograph that had inspired him, but suited the actual space. A successful idea sometimes needed to become smaller when practical responsibilities were taken into account.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Growing plants together creates opportunities for neighbours to talk. It also requires decisions about water, space and time. A successful community garden does not depend only on a good harvest. It depends on fair arrangements that allow people with different abilities to take part.
translation.referenceAnswer: 一起种植植物为邻居们创造了交谈机会，也需要大家就水、空间和时间作出决定。成功的社区花园不仅取决于收成好不好，还取决于是否有公平的安排，让能力不同的人都能参与。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Propose a shared garden for a residential area. Explain how work and harvests would be shared, including a way to settle disagreements.
writing.sampleAnswer: A shared garden could make our residential area greener and give neighbours a place to work together. I suggest assigning tasks through a flexible rota, with members able to exchange times when work or family duties change. People who cannot dig could sort seeds, keep records or help organise harvests. Produce should be shared through an agreed system, including labelled portions for members who arrive later in the day. If disagreements arise, two rotating representatives could listen to both sides and bring the issue to a short group meeting. The rules should be written clearly and reviewed after the first season. A good harvest would be welcome, but fair participation would be the more important sign of success.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
